question: Who competes with BSP for home-services deals?
html:
Home-services deal competitors

BSP's main rivals for home-services deals are national HVAC and plumbing consolidators and four sponsor-backed buyers already active in Punctual Pros' PA/NJ counties. They are not all equally able to bid. The scaled groups are well financed, while several next-tier groups are under debt pressure (Private-equity landscape; Competitor filings).

Local buyers in PA/NJ

RivalBackerBidding posture
Sila ServicesGoldman SachsHealthy. 2,500+ employees, est. $450–650M revenue (low confidence), growth almost entirely from acquisitions
Legacy Service Partners / HL BowmanGridiron (Fund V $2.1B)Scaled, borrows at par
Ally ServicesWatchtowerBuying in or next to Punctual Pros' counties
NorthwindsTruArcBuying in or next to Punctual Pros' counties
Horizon ServicesLender-owned by 2026Stressed. At least $211M first lien at Blue Owl, 3.75% PIK, marked 92.5

Sources: Private-equity landscape; Competitor filings; Home-services company case studies.

Haller (Lancaster, 254 trucks) is a healthier local rival. Its ownership is not stated in the context (Competitor filings).

National consolidators

These groups set add-on pricing (Private-equity landscape):

  • Apex, backed by Alpine. It did 46 add-ons in 2023 and 60 in 2025.
  • Wrench, backed by LGP.
  • TurnPoint, backed by OMERS.
  • Redwood, backed by Altas.
  • Any Hour, backed by Knox Lane.
  • T3, backed by Riverside.

Financial strength splits these groups in two (Competitor filings):

  • Well financed: Wrench, Apex, Redwood and Legacy borrow at S+425–475, marked at par, with delayed-draw lines for acquisitions.
  • Under pressure: TurnPoint, Horizon, Any Hour and Len the Plumber pay part of their interest in kind (PIK) and are marked at 89–94.
  • Near-term maturity: Heartland's debt matures Dec 15, 2026.

Horizon and Heartland are therefore more likely to sell assets or be restructured than to bid aggressively for add-ons (Competitor filings).

Fund-level competitors

  • BSP's Fund I is about $335M. Rivals run flagship funds of $0.9–2.1B, including Trivest VII at $950M and Gridiron V at $2.1B (Private-equity landscape).
  • MidOcean is the closest thesis peer. It covers franchise services and runs $50–300M+ equity checks (Private-equity landscape).

Where BSP can win

  • Avoid auctions. Focus on proprietary outreach to shops below $3M EBITDA that large-cap sponsors skip (Private-equity landscape).
  • Use the franchise system. Punctual Pros can offer Authority Brands territory rights and brand conversion (Private-equity landscape).
  • Data gap on pricing. The context has no add-on multiples paid in PA/NJ. Closed-deal comps or banker indications would be needed to quantify the pricing gap.

Next actions

  1. Build a target list of sub-$3M EBITDA PA/NJ shops. Prioritise those contiguous to Punctual Pros' counties.
  2. Monitor Horizon and Heartland for carve-outs or lender-led sales ahead of Dec 15, 2026.
  3. Gather recent PA/NJ add-on multiples to benchmark BSP bids against Sila, Legacy and Ally.
  4. Confirm which Authority Brands territory rights are available for conversion targets.
